sources: Lerer, Y. 2012. Horbat Qana, Survey. HA-ESI 124 (19 August 2012), Final Report, site list 1-34 and Fig. 1 (survey map). https://www.hadashot-esi.org.il/Report_Detail_Eng.aspx?id=2048
Site numbers used: 16, 20, 21, 23, 28
why: Site 20 is the only tomb west of the wall remains within 80-120 m (200 cubits at 0.40-0.60 m); its opening is on its eastern side.

sources: Lerer, Y. 2012. Horbat Qana, Survey. HA-ESI 124 (19 August 2012), Final Report, site list 1-34 and Fig. 1 (survey map). https://www.hadashot-esi.org.il/Report_Detail_Eng.aspx?id=2048
Site numbers used: 20, 21, 22, 23, 28
why: Written from site 22 (58 m, opening north). Without the opening, sites 21, 22 and 28 are all tombs west of the wall at 48-72 m. Even with it, sites 21 (70 m) and 22 (58 m) both fit: the cubit range cannot separate them.

sources: Lerer, Y. 2012. Horbat Qana, Survey. HA-ESI 124 (19 August 2012), Final Report, site list 1-34 and Fig. 1 (survey map). https://www.hadashot-esi.org.il/Report_Detail_Eng.aspx?id=2048
Site numbers used: 14, 16, 20, 28, 34
why: Written from site 34 (199 m at 65 deg, opening west), which is left out. Site 16 (191 m at 100 deg) is another tomb east of the wall at the same distance; it fits the instruction but is not the feature.

sources: Aladjem, E. 2014. Nahal Duda'im, Mishmar Ha-Negev Forest. HA-ESI 126 (6 December 2014), Final Report, sites 1-42 and Fig. 1 (location map and survey sites). https://www.hadashot-esi.org.il/Report_Detail_Eng.aspx?id=12657
Site numbers used: 12, 14, 15, 17, 21
why: Site 14 (554 m at 80 deg) and site 12 (526 m at 113 deg) are the only towers at 480-720 m; site 12 is attributed to the British Mandate (L). Site 14 lies east of the farm.

sources: Aladjem, E. 2014. Nahal Duda'im, Mishmar Ha-Negev Forest. HA-ESI 126 (6 December 2014), Final Report, sites 1-42 and Fig. 1 (location map and survey sites). https://www.hadashot-esi.org.il/Report_Detail_Eng.aspx?id=12657
Site numbers used: 12, 14, 15, 17, 21
why: With the Mandate attribution of site 12 removed (U), sites 12 and 14 are both towers east of the farm at 480-720 m, so the instruction cannot choose between them.

sources: Aladjem, E. 2014. Nahal Duda'im, Mishmar Ha-Negev Forest. HA-ESI 126 (6 December 2014), Final Report, sites 1-42 and Fig. 1 (location map and survey sites). https://www.hadashot-esi.org.il/Report_Detail_Eng.aspx?id=12657
Site numbers used: 12, 14, 15, 17, 21
why: Written from site 14, which is left out. The only other tower at 480-720 m is site 12, attributed to the British Mandate (L); the rest lie outside the distance band.

sources: Aladjem, E. 2013. Horbat Za'aq, Survey. HA-ESI 125 (1 October 2013), Final Report, opening paragraph (map ref. 18730/59132) and sites 1-39 within the ruin's precincts; Figs. 1-2. https://www.hadashot-esi.org.il/Report_Detail_Eng.aspx?id=4346
Site numbers used: 2, 20, 24, 28, 29
why: The report places site 2 'c. 200 m south of the ruin' and the instruction repeats that. Its map reference lies 283 m at 125 deg from the report's own map reference for the ruin, so the record and the words disagree; no other building lies south. The report records no entrance side.

sources: Aladjem, E. 2013. Horbat Za'aq, Survey. HA-ESI 125 (1 October 2013), Final Report, opening paragraph (map ref. 18730/59132) and sites 1-39 within the ruin's precincts; Figs. 1-2. https://www.hadashot-esi.org.il/Report_Detail_Eng.aspx?id=4346
Site numbers used: 12, 13, 15, 18, 21, 23
why: Written from site 21 (322 m at 79 deg). Six caves lie east of the ruin at 280-420 m; the instruction names nothing else that separates them. The report gives no entrance side for site 21's cave.

sources: Abu Raya, R. and Shapiro, A. 2011. Ahihud, 'Akko-Karmi'el Railway, Survey. HA-ESI 123 (26 December 2011), Final Report, sites 1-24 and Fig. 1 (survey map). https://www.hadashot-esi.org.il/Report_Detail_Eng.aspx?id=1925
Site numbers used: 5, 7, 14, 16, 20
why: Written from site 16 (150 m at 49 deg). Without the direction, site 7 (177 m, west) also lies at 120-180 m; site 20 has no recorded distance in this case. Its opening faces north-east.

sources: Hanna, B. 2012. Dabburiya, Har Devora, Survey. HA-ESI 124 (31 December 2012), Final Report, sites 1-11 and Figs. 1 (survey map), 9, 10, 12, 14, 18. https://www.hadashot-esi.org.il/Report_Detail_Eng.aspx?id=2179
Site numbers used: 4, 6, 8, 10
why: Site 4 is the large cave c. 10 m southeast of cave 3. A cardinal 'south' cannot be tested against a verbal south-east (quadrant edge), and no plan position exists: the report says site 4 is not marked on its map. Its opening apparently faces east.

sources: Hanna, B. 2012. Dabburiya, Har Devora, Survey. HA-ESI 124 (31 December 2012), Final Report, sites 1-11 and Figs. 1 (survey map), 9, 10, 12, 14, 18. https://www.hadashot-esi.org.il/Report_Detail_Eng.aspx?id=2179
Site numbers used: 3, 4, 6, 8, 10
why: Site 8 is the cave in the western part of the survey area whose opening faces south; the other caves open north or east.

sources: Abu Raya, R. and Shapiro, A. 2011. Ahihud, 'Akko-Karmi'el Railway, Survey. HA-ESI 123 (26 December 2011), Final Report, sites 1-24 and Fig. 1 (survey map). https://www.hadashot-esi.org.il/Report_Detail_Eng.aspx?id=1925
Site numbers used: 7, 13, 16, 20, 23
why: Site 16 is the only cave east of the kiln at 120-180 m. Site 7 lies west, so its missing distance does not matter.
